title: Rooted (Colossians 2:6–7)
hookLine: rooted and built up in him, overflowing with thanks
tomorrow: Paul tells the living 'ye are dead,' then hands them chores. why?

lines: THE FENCE FELL. THE OAK STOOD.
cards: The storm came through after midnight. By morning the new fence lay flat across two lawns, and the old oak beside it hadn't dropped a branch. Nobody had ever seen that oak's roots.

Now a letter is on its way to a small church in Colosse. The writer is in chains, and he says these people have never seen his face. Someone there talks smoothly, and he's worried they'll be carried off.
He warns them not to let anyone "beguile you with enticing words." You'd expect a long counterargument next. He writes two sentences.

teach.b: Here they are: "As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving."
Start with the first move. As you received, so walk. The way in is the way on; nothing new is needed to keep going.
Then two pictures in one breath.
Rooted is a tree word. Roots go down where nobody looks, and they keep a tree standing when the wind comes.

teach.h: BUILT UP: A WALL, COURSE BY COURSE.
teach.b: Built up is a building word, a wall rising course by course. Down and up at once. Then stablished, made firm.
Now look where the roots go. Not into a town, a house or a church building. In him.
Roots a person can carry. And the last word isn't about strength. It's thanks, abounding, running over like a cup.

teach.h: ROOTED IN HIM, NOT IN A PLACE.
teach.b: A rooted person in this letter isn't grim or stiff. It's someone steady enough to have thanks to spare.
So that's the answer to the smooth talker. Paul doesn't out-argue him. He tells them to go deeper where they already stand.

One to tell a friend tonight: near the end, Paul asks them to read this letter aloud, then send it on to the church in nearby Laodicea, and read the letter coming from there. Letters, passed hand to hand.

how: Some Christians memorize Colossians 2:6–7 as a short verse to come back to in unsteady times.

o: stuck in one place and unable to move on
proud of the town and family you came from
held from below, out of sight, so able to grow

p: a tree word: held from below

s: rooted means stuck in one place
Paul's roots go down in him, not in a town, so a person can carry them anywhere.
Paul answers the smooth talk with a long argument
he writes two sentences: walk as you received, rooted and built up.
abounding therein with thanksgiving: roots, a wall, and thanks running over.

games.q: your cousin is moving away for college and worries her faith won't survive without her home church. what does Colossians 2 say first?
o: as you received, so walk: go deeper where you already are, rooted in him.
find a church exactly like the one at home before anything else.
learn to win every argument there, so nobody can shake you.
games.why: Paul's answer to smooth talk isn't a better argument or the right building. it's roots in him, and thanks running over.

practice: Take your shoes off if you can, and stand or sit with your feet flat on the floor or the ground.
Let your weight sink down through your heels, as if roots were spreading from your soles, and on each breath out, let one thing you're thankful for come up.

wordCard.voice: Rooted. Paul's tree word in Colossians two: held from below, out of sight, in him, and so free to grow and give thanks.

carryVoice: Here's your line: rooted and built up, down out of sight and up course by course, at the same time. See you tomorrow.
